titleTag: What to Bring to Your US Visa Interview (and What Not To)
h1: What to Bring to Your US Visa Interview, and the List That Gets People Turned Away
deck: The documents are the easy half. The half that loses appointments is what you carry through the door: there is no cloakroom, no storage, and arriving with a phone and a backpack can end the visit before it starts.
metaDescription: What to bring to a US visa interview, plus the security rules that matter more: no electronics, no bags, no storage available, and what gets an appointment cancelled.

headline: No phone. No bag.
No storage.
coverSpec.title: US consulates prohibit electronics and large bags at the door and provide no facility to store them
coverSpec.desc: Battery-operated and electronic devices including mobile phones, smart watches, cameras, laptops, tablets and flash drives are not permitted at US embassies and consulates for visa interviews. Large bags, backpacks, briefcases and suitcases are prohibited, with only hand-carried folders of application papers allowed. There is no storage facility at the building or the visa application centre, and arriving with prohibited items can mean being refused entry and having the appointment cancelled.

faq.q: Can I take my phone to a US visa interview?
faq.a: No. Battery-operated and electronic devices are not permitted at US embassies and consulates for visa interviews, and that list includes mobile phones, smart watches, digital diaries, cameras, audio and video media, flash drives, memory sticks, Bluetooth devices, laptops, tablets and portable music players. There is no facility on site to store them, so you have to make an arrangement before you arrive.

faq.q: What happens if I arrive with prohibited items?
faq.a: You will not be allowed into the building, and consular guidance states that arriving with additional items can result in the appointment being cancelled. Because there is no storage at the embassy, consulate or visa application centre, that is not a problem you can solve at the door. It is the single most avoidable way to lose an appointment you waited months for.

Only something you can carry in your hand. Large shoulder bags, handbags, travel bags, backpacks, briefcases and suitcases are prohibited. What is generally permitted is an unsealed plastic bag, a small cloth bag or a zip folder containing your application papers. Pack for that constraint rather than planning to leave things somewhere.

faq.q: What documents do I actually need?
faq.a: At minimum, your passport, your printed DS-160 confirmation page with the barcode, your appointment confirmation with the correct current date, and a compliant photograph. Beyond that, bring what supports your stated purpose of travel and matches what your DS-160 says. Requirements vary by post and category, so check your own post's instructions as well.

faq.q: Do I need to print the DS-160 confirmation page?
faq.a: Yes. The barcode on the printed confirmation page is what identifies your application at the counter, and posts routinely refuse entry without the physical printout. Check that the barcode number matches the one linked to your appointment. If you submitted a second DS-160 to correct an error, bring both confirmation pages.

faq.q: Should I bring lots of supporting documents?
faq.a: Bring what is relevant and organised, not everything you own. A consular interview is short, and an officer will ask for what they want to see. A thick folder of unrequested paperwork does not improve a weak case and can make an organised one look anxious. The test is whether each document supports what your DS-160 already says.

Follow the time on your appointment confirmation, and expect a queue outside before security. Arriving very early rarely gets you seen sooner and often means standing in the open for longer. Arriving late can mean not being seen at all, which at a post with a long queue is an expensive way to lose a day.

cta.heading: Losing an appointment at the door is the worst way to lose one
cta.body: At a post where the next date is months away, being turned back over a phone or a backpack costs far more than the inconvenience suggests. This page exists so that does not happen to you. If it already has, or if you need to move an appointment for any other reason, our team can take the rescheduling work on. Tell us your post, your current date and the widest range you could accept, and we will tell you honestly whether it is worth paying us at all.
